name: Viktor Orbán
role: Prime minister of Hungary (1998–2002, 2010–2026); leader of Fidesz
summary: Leader of Fidesz and prime minister of Hungary. His governments have stressed national sovereignty, a family policy built on marriage between a man and a woman and on birth incentives, strict limits on migration, and close economic and diplomatic ties with China and Russia-linked energy projects. In a 2014 speech he described the state he was building as 'illiberal'; scholars describe the resulting system as a hybrid regime.

abortion-legal.rationale: His government kept the 1992 law allowing early abortion in a declared crisis while he personally opposes abortion; mixed evidence, so low.

basic-income.rationale: In 2019 he explicitly rejected income paid independently of employment.

central-planning.rationale: His illiberal programme explicitly retains the capitalist market economy.

close-ties-china.rationale: He has said Hungary was the first EU member state to join the Belt and Road Initiative and is an ideal pillar for it, while keeping Hungary in the Western military alliance rather than replacing it.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: His constitution narrowed judicial review in fiscal matters, but the evidence is partial and he also operated with a constitutional court; mixed, so low.

decent-living-guarantee.rationale: Warned that people who can live on benefits may choose them over work and that this undermines the economy, and his government tightened eligibility; he did not call for cutting welfare as such.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: In his 2019 Bălvănyos speech he rejects the claim that democracy is necessarily liberal, arguing that a state with democratic institutions and equal votes remains a democracy while pursuing illiberal, Christian-national policies.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: In 2021 he warned that the EU's climate package would destroy Europe's middle classes through energy prices; this opposes EU-level climate measures but he has not clearly rejected climate action itself.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He says individual freedom must not override community interests (2019 address), but does not speak of duties coming before rights.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He rejects closed East–West blocs and wants Hungary to connect both economies.

elite-replacement.rationale: In 2019 said that some political forces want population replacement and in 2018 said that some people would bring in millions from other ethnic groups to transform Europe; he did not name elites or assert deliberate promotion of migration by them in the same terms.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: Argued that the constitution must protect Hungary from international organisations and EU decisions that he described as anti-family, and opposed UN-based migration arrangements.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He advocates preserving European national populations against extra-European demographic mixing.

expand-nuclear.rationale: His government signed the 2014 Paks II agreement to expand Hungary's nuclear power plant.

flat-income-tax.rationale: His government introduced a flat 16% personal income tax in 2012, replacing progressive taxation in 2015.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: He condemns the 1956 Soviet intervention that crushed Hungary's attempt to leave the Soviet bloc as occupation, celebrating those who 'attacked the Soviet tanks' and lamenting that Hungary was 'abandoned to our fate'.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He rejects the proposed integration of large Muslim populations with indigenous Christian society.

legalize-drugs.rationale: He announces zero tolerance toward rising drug consumption and orders an enforcement campaign.

limit-population.rationale: He rejects fewer births as environmental policy and urges planning for growing populations.

more-religion-public.rationale: Said in 2017 that Christianity must regain its strength in Europe, and his government drove a programme to re-Christianize schools and expand religion's role in public education.

nation-first.rationale: Places national sovereignty at the centre of his politics, and rejects EU-level decisions that override national constitutional choices.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Said Hungary's constitution must protect the country against EU decisions and that courts should not override the national constitutional order on family policy.

open-borders.rationale: Rejects migration as a way of solving population decline and opposes EU compulsory migrant quotas; this is a rejection of the idea that borders should eventually open.

party-commands-army.rationale: He expressly orders the military to remain above party politics.

party-controls-media.rationale: Record: allies consolidated hundreds of outlets into the pro-government KESMA foundation and public media follows the government line; the record wins.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: Remains in the EU but opposes deeper pooling of sovereignty, rejecting federal-style integration and arguing that EU decisions can threaten national family policy.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: Describes national identity, cultural heritage and the 'national foundations' of family policy as things the state should protect, and summarised his 2014 illiberal programme as including preservation of cultural heritage.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: He defends food price freezes and continuing intervention against food-price inflation.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Argued that Europe must rebuild its birth rate through a family support system that makes having children financially better for parents, and rejected immigration as a substitute.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: The 1999 status law, passed under his first government, provided education, health and employment benefits for ethnic Hungarians in neighbouring states, and he has continued this line.

public-service-media.rationale: He expects public broadcasting to lean toward the conservative government, rather than remain politically independent.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: He endorses a further substantial rise, citing the 11 percent increase and his continuing wage programme.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Presents border barriers and the rejection of migration as the answer to Europe's demographic problem as core government policy, and in 2023 said that 'secure borders' had been abandoned by Brussels.

religious-nation.rationale: He makes preserving Christianity a condition for continued national existence.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: His government attacked George Soros and the NGOs he funds from 2017, framing them as a threat to national sovereignty; the Wikipedia summary does not record the exact legal measures, so the level is low.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Supported domestic legislation restricting same-sex marriage, and the 2011 constitution defines marriage as between a man and a woman.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: At the 2017 memorial for victims of communism he regretted that, unlike Nazism's crimes judged by an international military court, communism's crimes never received a similarly strict verdict, and said they cannot be excused.

separated-powers.rationale: He recognises independent courts, but his constitutional project substantially curtailed fiscal judicial checks.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: He told dpa in 2021 that children's sexual education is their parents' job 'under any circumstances', defending the 2021 law that restricts what schools may teach on sexuality.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He calls for spiritual renewal and intellectual foundations for family policy; he does not state a view about human nature having a spiritual and material side.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He personally sponsors strategic nuclear investment and his new-factory industrial programme.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: His strategy explicitly retains the Western military alliance while seeking Eastern economic links.

student-debt-relief.rationale: He announced loan cancellation only for mothers of several children, a narrow policy rather than relief for graduates generally.

traditional-family.rationale: Said in 2019 that every child has the right to a mother and a father, and that Hungarian family policy supports and protects the traditional family model.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Argued that family allowances should be tied to employment, warning that benefits can lead people to live on welfare rather than work, and his government linked benefits to work.

notes:
Views changed: as a young liberal and anti-communist founder of Fidesz (late 1980s to 1990s) he held positions that are not used here; answers reflect his positions from roughly 2010 to 2025. Two of his key speeches are covered only by secondary reporting: the 2014 Băile Tușnad speech (summarised in Wikipedia; the full English text was not reachable) and the 2022 Băile Tușnad remarks (Insight Hungary). Answers that rely on them are medium at most. Judgment calls: elite-replacement was answered +1 rather than +2 because he speaks of 'political forces' and 'people' rather than elites; discourage-race-mixing and diversity-weakens-cohesion were left null as nearby but not matching; restrict-foreign-funding and party-controls-media were set at +1 low because they rest on contested record evidence.

Merged with an independent gpt-6.1-sol audit: 30 answers taken from it, 18 agreed, 0 conflicts settled by the integrator.

gpt-6.1-sol notes: Independent research under the October 28 source-priority rules. No existing answers copied; no living-person inferences. The 2026 election observation documents substantial incumbent advantages, while the subsequent transfer of power prevents treating Hungary as a closed single-party state. Criticism of EU integration is not opposition to all international cooperation. Cross-border national solidarity is not a territorial annexation demand. Immigration and mixed-society rhetoric does not explicitly settle the separate proposition about interracial marriage and childbearing. Personal moral opposition to abortion is distinguished from his explicit 2022 support for retaining its broad legal framework. The original 2014 speech endpoint, current prime-minister site and original EUR-Lex judgments were unavailable; none is cited as read. Court findings below use the court’s own press account. The 2011 constitutional text is used only with his personal ownership of that constitutional project, not to attribute every clause. All remaining nulls reviewed against the complete 490-statement list.

claude-opus-5-5 deepening pass (2026-10-31), on line 12: searched the official English archive of 2015-2022.miniszterelnok.hu (23 October 1956 anniversary speeches 2016-2021, Bălvănyos 2018/2019/2022, Memorial Day for the Victims of Communism, the police centenary and military swearing-in speeches, journalists' Q&A) for revolution, the 1956 Soviet intervention, democracy, accountability for communist crimes, surveillance/Pegasus, terrorism, language for immigrants, trade surplus, martyrs and foreign bases. Added intervene-in-bloc, democracy-is-procedure and security-forces-accountable. Nothing of his own found on surveillance (the Pegasus record is the government's claim of legality, not his position on the statement), martyrs (he honours 1956's 'heroes', which does not settle 'martyrs and saints'), immigrants' language, trade surplus or foreign bases. Rules 3 re-sourcing: sex-ed-in-schools and close-ties-china re-sourced to his office's reports (close-ties-china lowered to +1 medium: the source shows close ties with China alongside, not instead of, the Western alliance); no-religion-state-schools, patriotic-education and gender-identity-recognition cited only Wikipedia and are null until a pass cites the laws or his words. The 2014 Tusnádfürdő speech and the 1989 Nagy reburial speech could not be fetched (the 2010-2014 government page is gone and miniszterelnok.hu is under reconstruction).
